key_insight: A reduced-basis TBNN-UDE hybrid can learn frame-invariant viscoelastic constitutive laws from shear-only data and still generalize to more complex extensional and benchmark flows.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical path to digital twins for viscoelastic fluids, enabling learned constitutive models to be embedded directly into CFD solvers for predictive simulation.
method: Train on synthetic oscillatory-shear datasets from established viscoelastic models.
Use a reduced dimensional tensor-basis formulation to improve physical consistency and numerical stability.
Embed the UDE into an open-source finite-volume solver for runtime constitutive evaluation.
evidence_signal: The models were tested by extrapolating from shear training data to unseen extensional, 2D, and 3D benchmark flows, including 4:1 sudden contraction and cross-slot cases, with accuracy improving when first normal stress difference information was added.
watch_item: Performance degrades as extrapolation increases, so stability and accuracy in strongly out-of-distribution flows remain a key implementation concern.
paper_title: Harnessing Machine Learning for Hybrid Constitutive Modelling of Viscoelastic Fluid Flows in Computational Rheology
